results.title: Coherent group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group is coherent if all of its finitely generated subgroups are finitely presented.

results.title: Coherent ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A semiring $R$ is (left) coherent if every finitely generated left ideal of $R$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module.

results.title: One-relator group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group `G` is called one-relator if it has a presentation with a single relation.

results.title: Jaikin-Zapirain–Linton theorem: one-relator groups are coherent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a one-relator group and $K$ a field. Then $G$ is a coherent group and the group algebra $K[G]$ is a (left) coherent ring.

results.title: Profinite completion
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The profinite completion of a group $G$ is the inverse limit of the finite quotient groups $G/N$, where $N$ ranges over the normal subgroups of finite index in $G$ and the maps are the quotient maps $G/N \to G/M$ for $N \le M$. It is a profinite group.

results.title: Profinitely rigid group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $\Gamma$ is *profinitely rigid* if it is finitely generated and residually finite, and $\Gamma$ is isomorphic to every finitely generated residually finite group $\Lambda$ whose profinite completion is isomorphic, as a group, to the profinite completion of $\Gamma$.

results.title: Ring of integers of a field obtained by adjoining a square root to $\mathbb{Q}$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $d$, the ring of integers of the number field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})$, realized as the splitting field of $X^2 + d$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

path: Fractional ideals prime to an ideal

results.title: Non-zero-divisors stay non-zero-divisors in a localization at a prime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal of $A$. Every non-zero-divisor of $A$ maps to a non-zero-divisor of the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$.

results.title: Fractional ideals prime to an ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. Then $I$ is prime to $J$ if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ with $J \subseteq \mathfrak p$, the extension $I A_{\mathfrak p}$ of $I$ to the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$, a fractional ideal of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ in $K$, is the unit fractional ideal $A_{\mathfrak p}$.

results.title: The unit fractional ideal is prime to every ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the unit fractional ideal $A$ of $A$ in $K$ is prime to $J$.

results.title: Products of fractional ideals prime to an ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. If fractional ideals $I$ and $I'$ of $A$ in $K$ are both prime to $J$, then their product $I I'$ is prime to $J$.

results.title: Inverses of invertible fractional ideals prime to an ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. If an invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$ is prime to $J$, then its inverse $I^{-1}$ is prime to $J$.

results.title: Invertible fractional ideals prime to an ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. The invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ that are prime to $J$ form a subgroup of the group of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$.

results.title: Membership in the subgroup of units prime to an ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. An invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$ lies in the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals prime to $J$ if and only if $I$ is prime to $J$.

results.title: Prime to an ideal implies prime to every larger ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$ and let $J \subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. If $I$ is prime to $J$, then $I$ is prime to $J'$.

results.title: Monotonicity of the subgroups of units prime to an ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J \subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. Then the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to $J$ is contained in the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to $J'$.

results.title: Every invertible fractional ideal is prime to the unit ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$. The subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to the unit ideal $A$ is the whole group of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$.

results.title: Permutation polynomial over a finite field
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A polynomial $f$ over a finite field $F$ is a permutation polynomial when its evaluation map $F \to F$, $x \mapsto f(x)$, is bijective.

results.title: Polynomial complete to level $k$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural number. The polynomial $f$ is complete to level $k$ ($k$-complete) when $f + iX$ is a permutation polynomial for every natural number $i \le k$, where $i$ is viewed as an element of $F$.

results.title: Unfolded form of $k$-completeness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural number. Then $f$ is complete to level $k$ if and only if for every natural number $i \le k$ the map $F \to F$, $x \mapsto (f + iX)(x)$, is bijective, where $i$ is viewed as an element of $F$.

results.title: Completeness at a lower level
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and let $j \le k$ be natural numbers. If $f$ is complete to level $k$, then $f$ is complete to level $j$.

results.title: Completeness at level zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $f \in F[X]$. Then $f$ is complete to level $0$ if and only if $f$ is a permutation polynomial.

results.title: Completeness at the next level
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural number. Then $f$ is complete to level $k + 1$ if and only if $f$ is complete to level $k$ and $f + (k + 1)X$ is a permutation polynomial, where $k + 1$ is viewed as an element of $F$.

results.title: A $k$-complete polynomial is a permutation polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $f \in F[X]$ and $k$ a natural number. If $f$ is complete to level $k$, then $f$ is a permutation polynomial.

results.title: Monomial permutation polynomials of a finite field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $d \ge 1$ be an integer. Then $X^d$ is a permutation polynomial of $K$ if and only if $\gcd(d, q - 1) = 1$.

results.title: Power-sum criterion for distinct elements of a finite field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $a_1, \dots, a_q \in K$. Then $a_1, \dots, a_q$ are pairwise distinct if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^{q} a_i^t = 0$ for every $t = 0, 1, \dots, q - 2$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{q} a_i^{q-1} = -1$, where $0^0 = 1$.

results.title: Shifted power-sum permutation polynomials of a prime field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $k, t, a$ be positive integers with $\gcd(a + 1, p - 1) = 1$ and $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$. Suppose that $p - 1 \nmid t$ or $p^2 \mid k - 1$. Then the polynomial $\sum_{n=1}^{k} n^t X^{n+a}$, with coefficients reduced modulo $p$, is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb{F}_p$.

results.title: Dilated power-sum permutation polynomials of a prime field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $k, t, a$ be positive integers with $p \nmid a$, $\gcd(a, p - 1) = 1$ and $k \equiv 1 \pmod{p(p-1)}$. Suppose that $p - 1 \nmid t$ or $p^2 \mid k - 1$. Then the polynomial $\sum_{n=1}^{k} (an)^t X^{an}$, with coefficients reduced modulo $p$, is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb{F}_p$.

results.title: Logarithm gap between a real number and its floor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real $x \ge 1$, the floor $\lfloor x \rfloor$ of $x$ satisfies $\log x - \log \lfloor x \rfloor \le 1/\lfloor x \rfloor$.

results.title: Explicit harmonic error bound at integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k$ be the $n$-th harmonic number and $\gamma$ the Euler–Mascheroni constant. For every natural number $n \ge 1$, $|H_n - \log n - \gamma| \le 1/n$.

results.title: Explicit harmonic error bound at real arguments
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k$ be the $n$-th harmonic number and $\gamma$ the Euler–Mascheroni constant. For every real $x \ge 2$, with $\lfloor x \rfloor$ the floor of $x$, $|H_{\lfloor x \rfloor} - \log x - \gamma| \le 2/x$.

results.title: Harmonic numbers at the floor track the logarithm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H_k$ denote the $k$-th harmonic number, $\lfloor x \rfloor$ the floor of a real number $x$, and $\gamma$ the Euler–Mascheroni constant. Then $H_{\lfloor x \rfloor} - \log x - \gamma = O(1/x)$ as $x \to \infty$.

results.title: Containing a copy of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A simple graph $G$ contains a copy of a simple graph $F$ if there is an injective map $f$ from the vertices of $F$ to the vertices of $G$ such that $f(u)$ and $f(v)$ are adjacent in $G$ whenever $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $F$; the copy need not be induced.

results.title: The extremal number of a graph

It is $0$ when every simple graph on these $n$ vertices contains a copy of $F$.

results.title: Erdős–Simonovits degeneracy conjecture (Erdős Problem 146)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every finite simple graph $H$ and every natural number $r \ge 1$, if $H$ is bipartite and $r$-degenerate (every nonempty set of vertices contains a vertex with at most $r$ neighbours in that set), then $\mathrm{ex}(n; H) = O(n^{2 - 1/r})$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathrm{ex}(n; H)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices containing no copy of $H$.

results.title: Counterexample to the Erdős–Simonovits degeneracy conjecture

results.title: 2CSP instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A 2CSP instance is a triple $(n, \Sigma, C)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of variables), a natural number $\Sigma$ (the alphabet size) and a finite list $C$ of constraints, where each constraint is a triple $(u, v, P)$ of natural numbers $u$ and $v$ (the variables it mentions) and a finite list $P$ of pairs of natural numbers (the allowed label pairs).

results.title: Well-formed 2CSP instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A 2CSP instance $(n, \Sigma, C)$ is well-formed when every constraint $(u, v, P)$ in $C$ satisfies $u < n$ and $v < n$, and every allowed pair $(a, b)$ in $P$ satisfies $a < \Sigma$ and $b < \Sigma$.

results.title: Satisfied constraint of a 2CSP instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $I = (n, \Sigma, C)$ be a 2CSP instance and $\sigma$ an assignment of a label less than $\Sigma$ to each variable less than $n$. A constraint $(u, v, P)$ is satisfied by $\sigma$ when $u < n$, $v < n$ and the pair $(\sigma(u), \sigma(v))$ belongs to $P$.

results.title: Value of a 2CSP instance under an assignment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $I = (n, \Sigma, C)$ be a 2CSP instance and $\sigma$ an assignment of a label less than $\Sigma$ to each variable less than $n$. The value of $I$ under $\sigma$ is the rational number $1$ if $C$ is empty, and otherwise the number of entries of the list $C$ that are constraints satisfied by $\sigma$, divided by the length of $C$.

results.title: Degree of a variable in a 2CSP instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a 2CSP instance $(n, \Sigma, C)$ and a natural number $v$, the degree of $v$ is the number of entries $(u, w, P)$ of the list $C$ with $u = v$ or $w = v$.

results.title: Linear search
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and a list $L$ of elements of $\alpha$, linear search scans $L$ from the front and returns the index of the first element of $L$ that satisfies $p$, or no index if no element does, together with a cost that counts one unit for each evaluation of $p$. On the empty list it returns no index at cost $0$. On a list with head $x$ and tail $T$ it evaluates $p(x)$ at a cost of one…

results.title: Linear search returns the first satisfying index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$, the index returned by linear search for $p$ on $L$ (ignoring its cost) equals the result of the standard library's first-index search: the least $i < n$ with $p(x_i)$ true, or no index if $p(x_i)$ is false for every $i < n$.

results.title: Characterization of a successful linear search
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, every list $L = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $i$, linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns the index $i$ if and only if $i < n$, $p(x_i)$ is true, and $p(x_j)$ is false for every $j < i$.

results.title: Linear search fails exactly when no element satisfies the predicate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$, linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns no index if and only if $p(x)$ is false for every element $x$ of $L$.

results.title: Cost of linear search on the empty list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, linear search for $p$ on the empty list has cost $0$: it evaluates $p$ zero times.

results.title: Cost recurrence for linear search
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, every $x \in \alpha$ and every list $T$ over $\alpha$, the cost of linear search for $p$ on the list with head $x$ and tail $T$ is $1$ if $p(x)$ is true, and $1$ plus the cost of linear search for $p$ on $T$ if $p(x)$ is false. The head costs one evaluation of $p$, and the tail is searched only when the head fails.

results.title: Cost of a successful linear search
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, every list $L$ over $\alpha$ and every natural number $i$, if linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns the index $i$, then its cost is $i + 1$: it evaluates $p$ exactly $i + 1$ times.

results.title: Cost of an unsuccessful linear search
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$, if linear search for $p$ on $L$ returns no index, then its cost is the length of $L$: it evaluates $p$ once for every element of $L$.

results.title: Linear search costs at most the list length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$ and every list $L$ over $\alpha$, the cost of linear search for $p$ on $L$ is at most the length of $L$: it evaluates $p$ at most once for every element of $L$.
